transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Yeah, so… what brings me in is that I’ve been feeling like I’m constantly moving from one thing to the next. Like I can’t really just sit and idle, if that makes sense. Even when nothing urgent is happening, I feel like I have to be doing something or switching to something else.

And with the new setup at work, it’s gotten harder to sort of cover it up or work around it. I’m a customer service rep, so I used to be able to manage it in little ways, but now it feels more obvious and more difficult to keep contained. It’s not like I’m trying to be difficult or anything—I just feel like my engine is always running, and lately it’s been getting in the way enough that I thought I should finally come talk to someone.
Do you find it hard to focus or stay attentive, especially when you’re doing something that requires sustained mental effort, like reading or working on a task for a long time?

Yes, definitely. I mean, I can start out okay, especially if I’m trying to really pay attention, but it doesn’t hold very long. Like in the longer coaching meetings at work, I’ll be looking right at the person and nodding, and then a few minutes later I realize I didn’t really absorb what they just said. It’s not that I don’t care—it’s more like the words are going by, but they’re not sticking.

Same thing if I’m reading a new procedure or some updated instructions. My eyes keep moving down the page, so from the outside it looks like I’m reading, but then I get to the end of a section and think, “Wait, what did I just read?” Then I have to go back and reread it, sometimes more than once. It’s frustrating because I’m not trying to slack off, but sustained attention like that is hard for me.
Do you often feel restless or as if you need to be moving or doing something, even in situations where others might be comfortable sitting still, like during meetings or when relaxing at home?

Yeah, I do. It’s not like I’m jumping out of my chair every two seconds, but sitting still for too long makes me feel kind of… boxed in, I guess is the best way to put it.

Like if I’m watching a training video at work, especially one of those slower ones where you just have to sit there and absorb it, I start feeling this pressure to move. I’ll want to stand up, stretch, shift around, click a pen, mess with something in my hands—anything so I’m not just sitting there doing nothing. Same thing at a slow appointment, like if I’m waiting and everyone else seems fine just sitting quietly. I’m sitting there thinking, “How are you all just doing this?” It’s uncomfortable, like my body wants me to get up even if my head knows I’m supposed to stay put.

At home it can happen too if I’m trying to relax, but it’s more noticeable in places where I’m expected to sit still and be patient. I can do it, but it takes effort, and I’m usually fighting the urge to move around somehow.
When did you first notice these difficulties with restlessness and maintaining focus? Were they present during your childhood, like when you were in school?

Yeah, looking back, I don’t think this is something that just started with the new work setup. That’s just what’s making it harder to hide now, I guess.

When I think back to school—like grade school, not just high school—I remember it being there in some form. I wasn’t, you know, considered unable to learn or anything. The way it was usually put was that I was “bright but careless,” which I heard more than once. Teachers would say I could understand the work, but I’d make sloppy mistakes or not stay with it long enough. And I remember getting reminders to get back to my work, like I’d drift off or start doing something else before finishing.

I also got comments about talking out of turn. Not all the time like I was trying to be a problem, but enough that it showed up in what teachers said. It’s funny, because at the time I just thought that was my personality or that I needed to try harder. But now, with what’s happening at work, it kind of makes me realize this has probably been around for a long time.
Have there been times when you felt unusually energetic, more talkative than usual, or like your thoughts were racing, even if only for a few days at a time?

Um… I don’t think so, not in the way you’re describing. I mean, I can be talkative sometimes, especially if I’m interested in something or I get going on a topic, but I wouldn’t say I’ve had periods where I felt unusually energized for days or like my mind was racing in some big noticeable way.

I’d have to think about it, because sometimes it’s hard to judge what’s “more than usual,” you know? But nothing really stands out to me as a stretch of a few days where I was suddenly a totally different version of myself or had this burst of energy that other people would have noticed. If anything, I’m more aware of getting distracted or restless than having that kind of elevated feeling.

Do you often act on impulse or find yourself doing things without thinking them through, like interrupting others, making quick decisions you later regret, or starting new projects without finishing old ones?

Yeah… I think I do that, especially with interrupting or jumping in. I don’t mean it in a rude way, and I’m usually not trying to take over, but it happens.

At work, for example, if I hear one of my coworkers talking through a customer problem—like they’re trying to figure out what to tell the customer or they’re asking another person for help—I’ll hear the situation and my brain kind of goes, “Oh, I know the answer.” And before they’ve even finished explaining it, or before anyone has actually asked me, I’ll jump in with, “Oh, you need to do this,” or “Tell them this,” or whatever the answer is.

And sometimes I can tell right after that I probably should’ve waited, because they weren’t done talking or maybe they weren’t even talking to me. It’s not like I’m trying to be disrespectful. In my head it feels helpful, like I’m solving the problem quickly. But then I realize I interrupted the flow of what they were doing, and I feel awkward about it. I’ll kind of backtrack and say, “Sorry, I didn’t mean to butt in,” but by then I’ve already done it.

So, yes, that kind of impulsive speaking out happens. It’s more like the answer comes out before I’ve had the extra second to think, “Is this my conversation? Did they ask me?”
Do you also notice these same kinds of difficulties—like trouble focusing, feeling restless, or acting impulsively—in other parts of your life, like at home or when you’re with friends or family?

Yeah, I do notice it at home too. It’s not just work. I think work is where it causes the most obvious problems because there are people waiting on me or there’s a task I’m supposed to be doing, but at home it shows up in quieter things.

Like reading, for example. I’ll sit down thinking, “Okay, I’m going to relax and read for a while,” and then after a few minutes I’m shifting around, rereading the same part, or suddenly thinking of something I should get up and do. And it’s not always something important—it might be getting a drink, checking something in the other room, adjusting the thermostat, whatever. It’s like I can’t just stay settled with it.

Movies with my wife are another one. She can sit and watch a whole movie straight through, and I’m the one moving around, making little comments, pausing to ask something, or getting up for some random reason. I don’t always mean to be disruptive, and sometimes I don’t even realize how much I’m doing it until she gives me that look or says, “Are you watching this or not?” And I am watching it, sort of, but I’m also fidgeting or needing to move or talk.

So yeah, even in things that are supposed to be relaxing and quiet, I don’t always do great with just sitting still and staying with it.
